metaDescription: Six cordless lawn edgers from 20V trencher style units to 80V brushless models and a 2 in 1 trimmer, compared on blade, depth, wheel and battery platform.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 8 Inch edger is the pick for most yards because it ships with its own battery and charger, uses a brushless motor and has a curb wheel for straight cuts. The VEVOR 8.8 Inch is the value pick for a small lawn with short edges. Skip a dedicated edger if you only touch up edges a few times a year, since a 2 in 1 trimmer such as the WORX WG163 covers that job for less.
introParagraphs: A dedicated lawn edger cuts a clean vertical wall between grass and pavement, which a string trimmer turned on its side never quite manages. The tool is a small motor, a steel blade and a wheel that rides the curb, and the quality of each decides how crisp your lines look.

Cordless models swap the extension cord for a battery. That raises a question a corded tool never asks: which battery platform you are buying into. This guide compares edgers across voltage, depth, blade design and whether the battery is in the box.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 8 Inch Brushless Edger Kit, 4.0Ah battery

specList.label: Guide
specList.value: Curb wheel, tool free depth adjustment

products.description:
This is the complete package: a brushless 40V edger with a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, so there is nothing else to buy. The brushless motor runs cooler and wastes less energy as heat, which matters when you push a blade through compacted soil along a driveway.

An 8 inch steel blade cuts the edge, a curb wheel follows the pavement so the line stays straight, and tool free depth adjustment lets you change depth without a wrench. A sister listing of the tool only version quotes a no load speed of 6500 rpm. Compared with the Greenworks 80V it is the kit that includes everything, and compared with a 20V trencher style edger it has more torque for overgrown borders.

Care is simple: remove the battery after use, scrape soil from the blade housing so it cannot cake and overheat, and inspect the blade for rounding after cutting along concrete. Store the pack indoors and partly charged. For the first pass along an overgrown edge, set the depth shallow and then drop it a notch for the second pass, which lets the motor work through roots without stalling and spares the battery from a hard bog down. Wear eye protection, because a blade at the pavement line throws grit.
products.bestFor: Most homeowners who want a complete cordless edger with no extra purchases.
pros: Curb wheel keeps the line straight
cons: 40V pack does not fit other brands

products.name: Greenworks 80V 8 Inch Brushless Edger, tool only

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Cordless dedicated blade edger, bare tool

products.description:
The 80V line is the high power end of Greenworks cordless, and this bare tool is for owners who already have the batteries. Five position depth adjustment gives the finest steps of any edger here, and the curb wheel keeps the cut parallel to the pavement. The listing says it cuts through compacted soil and concrete curbs with precision.

It is a tool only product, which means a battery and charger from the 80V family are extra. That is a poor buy if you start from nothing, and a smart one if you have a mower or blower on the same platform. Against the 40V kit it offers more motor headroom, and it costs more to enter.

Because the motor is brushless, there are no brushes to wear, so maintenance is mostly the blade. Keep the housing clear of packed soil, inspect the blade after concrete work and store the 80V battery inside through winter. Because the platform is shared with other 80V tools, a single large pack can serve a mower, blower and edger, which is the real economy of buying into the system. Make sure you note which charger fits, since the 80V and 40V chargers are not interchangeable.
products.bestFor: Owners already on the Greenworks 80V battery system.
pros: Five position tool free depth control
cons: High cost to enter the platform

products.name: WORX WG898.9 20V 7 Inch Brushless Edger, tool only

specList.label: Type
specList.value: Cordless dedicated blade edger, bare tool

specList.label: Guide
specList.value: Edge guide, blade indicator, dual wheels

products.description:
Seven pounds without the battery is the point of this edger. It is the lightest dedicated blade model here, and the dual wheels with an edge guide and a blade indicator keep it tracking along a border. The listing describes a uniquely streamlined blade, and the motor is brushless.

A 7 inch blade cuts a narrower and shallower trench than the 8 inch Greenworks tools, which is fine for tidying existing edges but less suited to restoring a lost border. It sells as a tool only unit, so you need a WORX 20V battery, which is a common platform across many of the brand's tools. Against the goodjob 20V edger it offers a known brand and a lighter feel, at the cost of battery and charger.

Store it with the battery removed, brush soil off after each use and check the blade indicator for alignment after a bump. It suits small lawns and light touch up work. Because the blade is narrower, plan on two passes for an edge that has been neglected for a season, and keep a spare blade in the shed, since a thin blade wears faster against concrete than a thick one.
products.bestFor: Small yards and anyone who wants a light edger on a 20V platform.

products.name: goodjob 20V Cordless Lawn Edger, 9 inch blade, 2 batteries
products.description:
A bundle that includes two 2.0Ah batteries and a fast charger is the draw. You can swap packs while one charges, which makes it far less likely that a half edged lawn ends because of a dead battery. A 400W motor spins the 9 inch steel blade at 3500 rpm, and three cutting depths with dual guide wheels shape the trench.

The larger blade gives more cutting reach than the 7 and 8 inch models, and the dual guide wheels add stability. It is a newer brand, so long term durability and parts support are less certain than for the Greenworks and WORX units. Against the VEVOR it has two batteries and a bigger blade, and against the WORX WG898 it ships ready to use.

Keep the blade clean and watch its fastener, since a lock tight arrangement should be checked for tightness every few uses. Charge both packs after each outing and store the tool dry. A small tip is to number the packs with tape and alternate them, so that wear is shared evenly and one does not end up with a weaker cell than the other.
products.bestFor: Budget minded homeowners who want two batteries and a big blade.
pros: Two 2.0Ah batteries and a fast charger
cons: Newer brand with a short track record

products.name: VEVOR 8.8 Inch Cordless Lawn Edger, 20V, 4000mAh battery
products.description:
This edger has three clearly stated depth settings, 1, 1.25 and 1.5 inches, which makes it easy to match the cut to grass height and soil hardness. An 8.8 inch blade handles driveway and sidewalk edges, and a 4000mAh battery pack drives it up to 3200 rpm.

It sits at the lower end of the price range, which makes it a sensible choice for a small yard with short edges. The depth range tops out at 1.5 inches, shallower than the Greenworks tools, so it is best for maintaining a border rather than cutting a new one. It undercuts the goodjob on price, with one battery instead of two and a smaller blade.

Remove the battery after use, scrape soil from the housing and check the blade for wear. A single pack means a long edging job may need a recharge before you finish. Before you buy, compare the full length of your edges to the depth and runtime you expect, because a driveway and two walks can easily be more than one pack covers on the deepest setting.
products.bestFor: Small lawns with short edges where cost matters.

products.name: WORX WG163 20V 12 Inch 2 in 1 Trimmer and Edger
products.description:
This is not a blade edger. It is a string trimmer whose head tilts 90 degrees so it can edge as well, and push button command feed advances the line without bumping. That gives you one tool for trimming and a passable edge for a light job, which is why it earns a place for people who edge only occasionally.

A string edge is less crisp and shallower than a steel blade trench, and it throws more debris, but it handles a lawn that only needs a tidy line. Against the dedicated models, it is lighter and costs far less, and it shares the WORX 20V battery with other tools. If you want the clean vertical wall, step up to a blade edger.

Change the line when it thins, keep the guard clean and store the tool with the battery removed. When you tilt the head to edge, check that the guard sits low enough to shield your shins, and keep the line at the length the guard allows, since an overlong line strains the motor.
products.bestFor: Occasional touch ups where one tool must trim and edge.
pros: Lower cost than a blade edger
cons: Edge is less crisp than a steel blade
Not for restoring a lost border

buyingCriteria.explanation: A steel blade edger like the Greenworks 40V cuts a vertical trench with a clean wall, while a tilting trimmer like the WORX WG163 flicks line along the edge. The blade gives a crisper, deeper result, and the string is gentler and more versatile. If you want a sharp border, buy a blade edger; if you want one tool, buy the 2 in 1.

Cordless tools lock you into a battery family. The Greenworks 80V and 40V are different platforms, the WORX models use 20V, and the goodjob and VEVOR use their own 20V packs. Count what you already own before you buy, because a tool only unit like the WG898.9 is cheap only if you have the pack.

Depth sets how well the edger can restore a border. The VEVOR cuts up to 1.5 inches and the Greenworks 80V offers five tool free positions. A deeper trench is better for a neglected edge, and a shallow one is fine for upkeep. Look for tool free depth adjustment.

A brushless motor is cooler and wastes less energy, giving more runtime from the same battery. The Greenworks and WORX WG898 are brushless. On a hard curb edge, that efficiency matters more than a high rpm figure, because soil drag is what drains a battery.

A curb wheel on the Greenworks and dual wheels on the goodjob and WORX keep the blade parallel to the pavement. A straight edge is mostly a tracking problem. Check the wheel width and whether the guide can be adjusted for lawns without curbs.

The WORX WG898.9 is about seven pounds without a battery, which is easy to push for twenty minutes. Heavier units tire your wrists. If you have long edges, choose the lighter tool and plan a second battery.

howWeEvaluated.description: Brushless motors and battery arrangement were compared. The Greenworks kit with its own pack was rated higher for a start from scratch buyer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tracking and guide wheels
howWeEvaluated.description: Curb wheels, dual wheels and edge guides were counted. The Greenworks curb wheel and WORX dual wheels led on straight lines.

faq.q: Is a cordless edger as good as a gas edger?
faq.a: For home lawns, a brushless cordless edger cuts a clean line and is quieter and easier to start. Gas edgers have more sustained power on very long borders.

faq.q: Which battery platform should I choose?
faq.a: Choose the one you already own. If you own none, a kit like the Greenworks 40V includes its own pack.

faq.q: How deep can a cordless edger cut?
faq.a: Depth varies by model. The VEVOR cuts up to 1.5 inches, and larger 8 inch tools cut deeper. Check each listing.

faq.q: How often should I replace the blade?
faq.a: Replace it when the edge is rounded or the cut turns ragged, often after a season of concrete edging.

faq.q: Can a string trimmer edge as well as a blade edger?
faq.a: It can tidy an edge, but it is less crisp and shallower. A blade edger gives a cleaner wall.

faq.q: How long does a battery last on an edger?
faq.a: It depends on soil and depth. A short border may use a fraction of a pack, and a neglected one may need two.
